page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 768 GB of RAM, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 5669 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

In benchmark evaluations, the E96ds_v6 demonstrates top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, achieving 506.7 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 207.77 GB/sec for writes. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU score of 93,126.45 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 20,410.0. Database operations and key-value store performance are highly efficient, with Redis SET operations reaching 122.52 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring in the top decile. The hardware also shows strong capabilities in cryptographic execution, physics simulations, and prompt processing for large language models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E96ds_v6 offers high resource density by combining substantial memory capacity with a large local storage footprint, reducing the need for external storage attachments in data-intensive tasks. The absence of a dedicated GPU makes it a cost-effective choice for CPU-bound and memory-bound enterprise workloads rather than heavy graphics processing. This server type is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
